brief: a short drama scene: a mother finds a letter her son left before moving away
concept: A morning like every other until the second cup she pours has no one to drink it.
plan_outline: 1. WS · eye · static · small kitchen, early morning window light · a woman in her fifties in a cotton sari makes tea for two (6 s)
2. CU · eye · static · same kitchen · two cups filled; she pauses at the second (4 s)
3. MS · eye · static · son's empty room, same light · a made bed, an envelope on the pillow (5 s)
4. CU · top · static · same room · her hand picks up the envelope (handwriting soft and unreadable) (4 s)
5. CU · eye · push in · same room · she reads; her face holds, then breaks into a small smile and tears (8 s)
6. WS · eye · static · kitchen · she sits at the table and drinks from the second cup (6 s)
why: The idea lives in one gesture (the second cup) set up in shot 2 and paid off in shot 6 — a motif, not dialogue.
Coverage moves from wide to close for the turn, then back to wide for the release.
Static frames and one slow push-in: drama earns the move at the emotional peak.
The letter's words are never shown (the model can't write them); her face reads them for us.
